Given rectangular coordinates \((x,y,z)=(2,-1,-2)\), use the standard spherical conversion:
\[
x=\rho\sin\phi\cos\theta,\quad y=\rho\sin\phi\sin\theta,\quad z=\rho\cos\phi.
\]

First find \(\rho\):
\[
\rho=\sqrt{2^2+(-1)^2+(-2)^2}=\sqrt{9}=3.
\]

Also,
\[
\cos\phi=\frac{z}{\rho}=\frac{-2}{3},
\]
so
\[
\sin\phi=\sqrt{1-\cos^2\phi}=\sqrt{1-\frac49}=\frac{\sqrt5}{3}.
\]

From \(x=2\),
\[
2=3\sin\phi\cos\theta=3\cdot \frac{\sqrt5}{3}\cos\theta=\sqrt5\cos\theta,
\]
so
\[
\cos\theta=\frac{2}{\sqrt5}.
\]
From \(y=-1\),
\[
-1=3\sin\phi\sin\theta=\sqrt5\sin\theta,
\]
so
\[
\sin\theta=-\frac{1}{\sqrt5}.
\]

Now for spherical coordinates \((\rho,\theta,2\phi)\):
\[
\cos(2\phi)=2\cos^2\phi-1=2\left(\frac49\right)-1=-\frac19,
\]
\[
\sin(2\phi)=2\sin\phi\cos\phi
=2\left(\frac{\sqrt5}{3}\right)\left(-\frac23\right)
=-\frac{4\sqrt5}{9}.
\]

Thus the new rectangular coordinates are:
\[
x'=\rho\sin(2\phi)\cos\theta
=3\left(-\frac{4\sqrt5}{9}\right)\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt5}\right)
=-\frac83,
\]
\[
y'=\rho\sin(2\phi)\sin\theta
=3\left(-\frac{4\sqrt5}{9}\right)\left(-\frac{1}{\sqrt5}\right)
=\frac43,
\]
\[
z'=\rho\cos(2\phi)
=3\left(-\frac19\right)
=-\frac13.
\]

The answer is \(\left(-\frac83,\frac43,-\frac13\right)\).
